animations: _MissedTurnsState._pulse — AnimationController 1100 ms, repeat(reverse: true); drives Opacity 0.72 + 0.28*v ONLY when you.onLastWarning; no curve applied.

_PotToWinnerState._c — AnimationController 1700 ms, forward() once; 9 chips, per-chip start = i/(9*1.6), Curves.easeInOutCubic, sin() arc of magnitude size*(1.4 + i*0.25) alternating sides, Transform.rotate ±2pi, opacity fade over the final 18 % (eased > 0.82). Wrapped in RepaintBoundary.
_PotChipsState._c — AnimationController 420 ms, forward(from: 0) only when widget.pot > old.pot; lift = sin(v*pi) -> translate(0, -6*lift) + scale(1 + 0.12*lift).
_Pot pot amount — TweenAnimationBuilder<double> 550 ms, Curves.easeOutCubic, counts up to room.pot.

_DealtState._c — AnimationController 380 ms started after Future.delayed(index * 110 ms); CurvedAnimation Curves.easeOutCubic driving FadeTransition + SlideTransition(Offset(-0.5,-0.9) -> zero) + ScaleTransition(0.85 -> 1.0).
_Banner — TweenAnimationBuilder<double> 520 ms, Curves.easeOutBack; scale 0.7 + 0.3*v and opacity v.
_SideshowLinkState._pulse — AnimationController 900 ms, repeat(); painter draws a bead at path length*t plus a ring at the asked seat radius 18 + 22*t fading with (1-t).

_SideshowCountdownState._frames — AnimationController 1000 ms, repeat(); used only as a per-frame tick — the level is recomputed from DateTime.now() vs expiresAt each frame. Colour = Color.lerp(error, secondary, (left*3).clamp(0,1)). RepaintBoundary.
_AmbientGlowState._breath — AnimationController 3800 ms, repeat(reverse: true), Curves.easeInOut; radius 0.55 + 0.08*v, alpha (dark 0.16 / light 0.12) + 0.08*v.

_BetFlightsState — a raw Ticker (createTicker), NOT an AnimationController; _travel 620 ms per flight, 70 ms stagger per simultaneously-launched seat, Curves.easeInOutCubic, sin(t*pi)*size*1.6 lift, Transform.rotate(t*pi*1.5), fade over the final 18 %. The ticker stops itself when _flights empties.
Fireworks._c — AnimationController 2600 ms, repeat(); 26 particles per burst, per-burst start offset, life window 0..0.55, (1-life)^2 fade, gravity term, blurred circles. RepaintBoundary.
PlayingCard._flip — AnimationController 420 ms, Curves.easeInOut, rotateY with 0.0015 perspective, face swaps at t > 0.5. Only fires on face-down <-> face-up (code null <-> non-null).
SeatPod._BlinkState._blink — AnimationController 780 ms, repeat(reverse: true), Curves.easeInOut; two breathing BoxShadows (blur 10+10t / 26+22t). Created LAZILY and nullable on purpose.
LiquidFill._wave — AnimationController 1800 ms, repeat(); two sine bodies + a crest stroke, level recomputed per frame from deadlineMs. RepaintBoundary.
SeatPod._lastBet figure — AnimatedSwitcher 280 ms, slide from Offset(0, 0.6) + fade, keyed ValueKey('<lastBet>-<isBlind>').
SeatPod._total — TweenAnimationBuilder<double> 450 ms, Curves.easeOutCubic.
SeatPod._Bubble — TweenAnimationBuilder<double> 220 ms, Curves.easeOutBack, scale 0.6 + 0.4*v anchored to the tail edge.
DriftingChips._clock — AnimationController 28 s, repeat().
PremiumSurface.Glint (available but NOT enabled anywhere on this screen) — 4200 ms travelling highlight.

GameState._ticker — Timer.periodic(1 s) calling notifyListeners(); every widget on this screen that calls context.watch<GameState>() rebuilds once a second. This is what refreshes turnProgress (pod colour) and chatCooldownLeft.
MaterialApp themeAnimationDuration 420 ms / Curves.easeOutCubic — the light/dark cross-fade the drawer's toggle triggers.
responsivenessBlockers: _SideRail: SizedBox(width: 46) — fixed; the felt's LayoutBuilder width is implicitly screen − safeArea − 46 − 24.
_TableDrawer: Drawer(width: 320); _ChatDrawer: Drawer(width: 340) — over half the screen on a 640 dp-wide landscape phone (TP_Small), unchanged on a tablet.
_Felt padding: EdgeInsets.fromLTRB(12, 2, 12, 0) — fixed 24 dp of horizontal felt margin at every size.
_Felt podW = min(h*0.30, w*0.155).clamp(56.0, 128.0) — the 128 dp ceiling means the felt stops scaling on a tablet; the 56 dp floor means pods collide on a very short screen.
_Felt handH = (h*0.29).clamp(50.0, 116.0) — same ceiling problem for the viewer's own cards.

_Felt._places is a hardcoded 5-entry List<Offset> of fractions; the bottom seat is special-cased to h*0.84 in _seatCentre and to bottom: h*0.035 in the Stack. No layout adapts to a different player count.
_Felt overlay slots are fixed fractions with fixed width fractions: tag at (0.5, 0.075) width w*0.30, pot at (0.5, 0.26) width w*0.34, status at (0.5, 0.44) width w*0.4.
Three different hardcoded pot positions that must agree: potCentre = Offset(0.5*w, 0.30*h) (bet flights), the _Pot widget at dy 0.26, and _PotToWinner from: Offset(0.5*w, 0.26*h).
_OwnHand horizontal offset: left = _places[0].dx * w + podW/2 + 8 — a bare 8 dp gutter.

_MissedTurnsStrip re-derives the felt geometry with magic numbers instead of reading it: screenW < 760 breakpoint; feltW = screenW − inset.horizontal − 46 − 24; feltH = size.height − inset.vertical − 64 (64 = an assumed action-bar height); podW formula duplicated verbatim from _Felt; podLeft = 46 + 12 + 0.335*feltW − podW/2 (0.335 is _places[0].dx re-typed as a literal); maxW = (podLeft − 16 − 20).clamp(120.0, 360.0); OverflowBox maxHeight 120.

_ActionBar: SizedBox(width: math.max(box.maxWidth, 760)) inside a FittedBox — on a 640 dp-wide device the whole bar is scaled to ~0.8, taking the 46 dp button height below 40 dp and under the 48 dp minimum touch target. Button widths are fixed: Pack 128, amount pill 148x46 (radius 23), Chaal 136, Show/Sideshow 132, gaps 10.

Chat drawer composer padding fromLTRB(16, 6, 16, 12) and list padding fromLTRB(16, 8, 16, 8) — fixed.
No MediaQuery.textScalerOf anywhere: every FittedBox hides a text-scale overflow by shrinking the text instead of reflowing.
doNotTouch: _TableScreenState.build deliberately subscribes to NOTHING (no context.watch). GameState ticks once a second; rebuilding this Scaffold tears down an open drawer mid-gesture. Adding `final state = context.watch<GameState>();` at the top of this build — the house convention everywhere else — silently breaks the chat and menu drawers.

The drawer GlobalKey comes from GameState.tableScaffold, not from a local key. main.dart's _BackGuard reads state.tableScaffold.currentState.isDrawerOpen / isEndDrawerOpen to close an open panel before it asks 'leave the table?'. A locally-created GlobalKey<ScaffoldState> makes the Android back gesture offer to leave the table whenever the chat is open.

A Scaffold has exactly one `drawer`. _panel is set (and setState'd) BEFORE openDrawer() is called; that ordering is why the correct panel is in the tree when it slides. Splitting menu and chat into drawer + endDrawer changes what the back guard closes first and collides with the lobby's endDrawer convention.
_open(_LeftPanel.chat) calls markChatRead() as a side effect. Drop it and the unread Badge never clears.

_Felt._seatCentre takes a SERVER seat index and rotates it into view order internally ((seatIndex − mine + total*2) % total). It is the shared source of truth for FOUR things: the sideshow link endpoints (sideshow.fromSeat/.toSeat), the fireworks focus, the pot-to-winner destination, and every bet flight's origin. Reordering _places, changing the rotation, or feeding it a view index instead of a server index makes all four animations point at the wrong player without any error.

_places must stay exactly 5 entries: _seatCentre does `_places[view % _places.length]`, so a 6th server seat would silently overlap seat 0 rather than fail. config.maxPlayers == 0 ? 5 : maxPlayers is the same assumption in seatsInViewOrder().
isMe is `s?.userId != null && s!.userId == state.user?.id`, NOT `viewIndex == 0`. When room.you is null the rotation falls back to identity and view seat 0 is somebody else. Do not 'simplify' this.

`reversed: viewIndex == 0` on the viewer's SeatPod reverses the whole pod column (cards and bet chip stack upward instead of down) — and the viewer's pod and hand are anchored by `bottom: h*0.035`, not centred like the rim seats, because their columns are different heights. Centring them re-clips both against the rim.

The `at()` helper clamps left to [0, w − box] and then applies FractionalTranslation(0, -0.5) so place.dy is a CENTRE. Removing either the clamp or the translation re-introduces the clipped outer pod on narrow screens.

handLive = betting || showdown || state.showdown.isNotEmpty || state.showdownResult.isNotEmpty. The last two terms are what keep seats showing their bets and statuses through the winner's celebration; dropping them makes every bet vanish the instant the server flips the table back to waiting. It is passed to every SeatPod and also gates the bet pills.

onTurn(s) requires room.state == TableState.betting AND s.seatIndex == room.turn.seatIndex. deadlineMs is handed to EVERY pod (room.turn?.deadline ?? 0); LiquidFill only renders under `onTurn && progress != null && deadlineMs > 0`. Loosening that condition puts a turn clock on the wrong seat.

_BetFlights is stateful and diffs Seat.contributed inside didUpdateWidget against a _seen map seeded in initState. It MUST remain the same element across rebuilds: giving it a key that changes, or wrapping it in `if (handLive)` / any conditional insertion, re-seeds the baseline and it will either replay the whole hand's bets or miss them. Its handNo check is what makes the boot fly at the deal.

_PotToWinner's key: ValueKey('pot-<handNo>-<winnerId>') is functional — it is what makes the flight run exactly once per win. Remove it and a second win in the same session never animates; make it change per rebuild and it restarts every frame.
_Dealt's key: ValueKey('<handNo>-<i>') is what re-triggers the deal animation on a new hand. Adding the card code to that key would destroy and recreate PlayingCard on every 'see', killing the flip.

_OwnHand always renders `for (var i = 0; i < 3; i++)` with `code: i < cards.length ? cards[i] : null`. Rendering only the cards that exist removes the three face-down backs a blind player must see, and destroys the see-cards flip (PlayingCard flips only on null <-> non-null).
_OwnHand's early return: `if (you.status != SeatState.active && !packed) return SizedBox.shrink()`, where packed = status packed || lost. Widening this shows a hand to a waiting/won seat.
stillBlind = you.isBlind && !packed gates the See button; state.see() is the only path to reveal. Note SEE is legal off-turn — do not gate the button on state.myTurn.

The action bar is ALWAYS present and only disables (comment at 2188 and CLAUDE.md §8.4). Making it appear/disappear moves keys under a thumb that is already committed — that is how misclicks happen on a 25 s clock.

headsUp = live && options.show != null && options.show > 0 is what turns the last slot from Sideshow into Show. options.show is null when a show is impossible; `?? 0` or a default would send a zero-cost show and the server refuses with insufficient_chips. The two can never be offered together (a show needs 2 players, a sideshow needs 3).
canSideshow is entirely the server's judgement (three in the hand, both seen, one ask per turn). Never compute it client-side; only mirror options.canSideshow.

The bet ladder index lives on GameState (raiseIndex), not locally: the room:state handler resets it to 0 on a new hand and clamps it to steps.length−1 on every snapshot. Keeping the stepper index in a local StatefulWidget makes the client offer a rung the server no longer has. Also GameState.bet() decides chaal vs raise by comparing to steps.first — the UI must not pick the action.
canStepDown / canStepUp already include myTurn. Re-deriving enablement from options.raiseSteps in the widget will drift.

_ActionBar's FittedBox contains a SizedBox(width: max(box.maxWidth, 760)) whose Row uses two Spacer()s. The SizedBox is what gives the Row a finite width — remove it and the Spacers throw inside the unbounded FittedBox.

_SideshowPrompt must NOT be wrapped in IgnorePointer (its two buttons are the only way to answer); _SideshowRevealPanel MUST stay wrapped in IgnorePointer (it is a passive overlay that would otherwise swallow taps for its 5 s life).

The reveal panel's guard is `sideshowReveal != null && showdown.isEmpty && showdownResult.isEmpty` — the winner's banner deliberately wins any race. Dropping the showdown terms stacks two full-screen panels.

_SideshowCountdown and LiquidFill both read DateTime.now() per frame rather than taking a level from GameState, precisely because the state republishes only once a second. Converting either to an AnimatedContainer/state-driven value reintroduces a stuttering, one-second-stepping clock. Neither corrects for clock skew — the deadline is the server's.

The felt Stack's paint order is load-bearing: glow, bet flights, category tag, pot, status, then the rim pods, then the bottom pod and own hand, then sideshow link/prompt/reveal, then showdown. Pods paint AFTER the tag/pot/status so a speech bubble or bet chip is never hidden behind a label. Reordering for 'z-index tidiness' hides the moments that matter.

SeatPod's speech bubble hangs in a zero-height OverflowBox off the END of the pod column so a player speaking never nudges their own pod, cards or chips; the bubbleSide (above for the viewer, right for view seats 1-2, left for 3-4) is what keeps bubbles pointing inward and off the rim. _MissedTurnsStrip uses the same zero-height OverflowBox trick so the action bar never shifts as the count changes. Both must keep SizedBox(height: 0).

seat_pod.dart's _BlinkState._c is nullable and lazily created ON PURPOSE, with a long comment. Converting it to `late final AnimationController` makes dispose() run the initialiser for the four pods that never blinked; the TickerMode lookup is illegal on a deactivated element and the throw lands inside _InactiveElements._unmount, surfacing much later as a duplicate GlobalKey / _ElementLifecycle assertion. Every table teardown hit this.
Seat.chips is nullable and null means WITHHELD (blind table), not zero — SeatPod renders '•••'. Any `?? 0` here leaks a lie about another player's stack.

_TableDrawer's leave/switch tiles call Navigator.pop(context) FIRST and only then show the dialog, so a dialog is never stacked on a drawer that is still sliding. _confirmSwitch awaits state.switchTable(); _confirmLeave calls the void state.leaveTable(). The mid-hand copy switch (room.state == betting && you.status == active) is requirement 25 and must survive.

_ChatDrawerState._send returns early when sendChat() returns false (blank text, or the 4 s client cooldown still running) — clearing the field before checking loses the message. On success it unfocuses AND pops the drawer, which is deliberate: the player should land back on the table with their words over their own seat.
The chat ListView is `reverse: true` and indexes `state.chat[state.chat.length - 1 - i]`. Changing one without the other silently flips message order.

state.colourFor(userId, scheme) derives the speaker colour from the SEAT INDEX (falling back to an id hash for someone who left) precisely because hashing ids gave two of five players the same colour. Do not replace it with a local hash.

_TableDrawer returns `const Drawer(child: SizedBox.shrink())` when room == null (the drawer can be open at the moment a kick lands) and _Felt returns a CircularProgressIndicator — both are real states, not dead branches.
_Status renders SizedBox.shrink when the computed text is empty (nobody to act). It reads room.minPlayers for the waiting line and room.turn.seatIndex via _nameOf, which requires seat.occupied.

winnerSeat is resolved by matching state.winnerId against room.seats — the winner may have LEFT, in which case winnerSeat stays null, the fireworks scatter (focus: null) and no pot flight is built. The `state.winnerPot <= 0` guard is the other half. Both branches must survive.

The three surfaces coloured by AppTheme.paletteFor (felt, category tag, and via palette.accent the glow, bet flights and sideshow link) are the player's only cue to which table they are on — blind vs seen, and 200 vs 5000 stake. On a BLIND table the palette is also the explanation for why every other stack shows '•••'. Flattening all tables to one emerald look removes a functional signal, not just a decoration.
GameConfig.fromJson coerces missing ints to 0, hence `config.maxPlayers == 0 ? 5 : …` and the `?? 4` on maxBlindMoves — keep those guards.

Every emit already carries a fresh actionId inside GameConnection.act; the UI must not add its own retry/debounce around pack/bet/show, and must not fire an action from a build or an animation callback.

doNotTouch: `onTap: capped ? () {} : () => context.read<GameState>().quickJoin(boot, category)` in _TableCard. The empty closure is NOT dead code — it is requirement 30's client-side refusal, and _Pressable's onTap is non-nullable so it cannot be null. The dimmed card underneath is still hit-testable (Opacity does not block pointers and the caption Container is not wrapped in IgnorePointer/AbsorbPointer), so any refactor that routes the tap to quickJoin for a capped table will send a join the server refuses and surface an error the player did nothing to earn.

The literal strings 'bonus' and 'milestone' passed to state.claimReward(...) are the REST path segment (POST /api/rewards/milestone|bonus). They look like UI identifiers. Renaming them, or deriving them from a translated label, breaks reward collection outright.

TableCategory.blind / 'blind' comparisons (`final blind = category == TableCategory.blind`) select the wording, the badge delay and the palette. The category string is server wire data — never normalise, capitalise, translate or store it back.

state.config.tables must be rendered verbatim, in the server's order, with no sorting, grouping, filtering or de-duplication. The server decides which (category, boot) pairs exist; two blind tables at different stakes are a deliberate menu, and inventing or hiding entries makes the lobby disagree with what quickJoin can actually reach.

_sampleIn(NumberSystem, GameState) mutates the module-level global chipNumberSystem, formats, and restores it — synchronously, inside build. It must stay synchronous and un-interleaved. Moving the formatting into a builder/Future/isolate, memoising it, or computing both samples concurrently leaves the global on the wrong system and every money figure in the whole app (table, seats, pot, store) formats wrong until the next setNumberSystem.

`key: state.lobbyScaffold` on the Scaffold is load-bearing: main.dart's _BackGuard walks [tableScaffold, lobbyScaffold] and closes an open drawer/endDrawer before it asks the quit question. Drop the key, or move the drawers off this Scaffold, and the Android back gesture asks 'quit the game?' while the settings drawer is open.

The single endDrawer slot plus `_open(context, panel)`: setState(_panel) and Scaffold.of(context).openEndDrawer() run in the same call, and the context passed in is _TopBar's (a descendant of the Scaffold). Splitting stats/settings into two Scaffolds, or calling Scaffold.of with _LobbyScreenState's own context (which is ABOVE the Scaffold), throws or opens the wrong panel.

_RewardCelebrationState._in is built in initState, deliberately not as a lazy `late final` field initialiser. build returns SizedBox.shrink() whenever rewardWon is null (nearly always), so a lazy controller would first be constructed inside dispose(), where the TickerMode lookup on a deactivated element crashes — the same bug already fixed in seat_pod.dart's _Blink. Do not 'tidy' it into a field initialiser.

_RewardCelebration is the receipt for an irreversible chip grant. dismissReward() is the only thing that clears it, it is reachable from both the full-screen scrim tap and the button, and the overlay is positioned last in the Stack so it covers the rail. Do not add a timeout, do not make it non-blocking, do not let the rail stay tappable behind it — a player who is unsure whether their tap worked taps again.

_shownFor compares won.amount, not identity: two rewards of the same amount in a row deliberately reuse the on-screen banner state. Keying an AnimatedSwitcher on the amount, or adding a key derived from it, changes when the entrance replays.

The whole lobby is driven by GameState's Timer.periodic(1s, notifyListeners) reaching context.watch<GameState>() in _LobbyScreenState.build, _TopBar, _BonusChip and _MilestoneChip. That per-second rebuild is what makes formatCountdown(r.untilBonus) tick and what flips r.bonusReady from waiting to collectable. Converting these to context.select, const subtrees, or memoised children freezes the four-hour countdown and leaves the bonus chip permanently disabled.

Conversely, no new AnimationController or now()-derived Tween may be constructed inside build on this screen — it is rebuilt every second, so anything created there restarts once a second. Every existing controller lives in a State and starts once.

Reward gating must stay on the server's booleans: r.milestoneAvailable and r.bonusReady (which is bonusAvailable || bonusReadyAt <= now). handsToNextMilestone reports 25, not 0, at an exact multiple — deriving 'ready' from `handsToNextMilestone == 0` makes the milestone unreachable. Likewise untilBonus is display only.

_BonusChip and _MilestoneChip return SizedBox.shrink() when user?.rewards is null (pre-login, mid-refresh). Replacing that with a placeholder card that has an onTap wired to claimReward will fire claims against a user whose rewards state is unknown.
Seat.chips-style nullability discipline applies to money everywhere: user?.chips ?? 0 is the only fallback in use; never render a withheld/absent value as a real 0.

_PrivateCard's TextField maxLength: 6 matches the server's room-code length (util.DefaultRoomCodeLength = 6). textCapitalization is cosmetic only — the actual trim + toUpperCase happens inside GameState.joinByCode. If a redesign uppercases in the field and drops joinByCode, or lengthens the field, codes stop matching.

createPrivate() sends category 'seen' from this client (the browser client sends 'blind'). The visible chip-visibility behaviour of a private table depends on it. Do not 'fix' the card's copy or add a category picker without changing the server-facing call deliberately.
Rules row order: Navigator.pop(context) FIRST, then showRules(context). Reversing them pops the dialog instead of the drawer.

_confirmDelete's `if (!context.mounted) return;` after await state.deleteAccount() is required — deletion has already switched Screen to login and torn this drawer's host down. The trailing Navigator.pop(context) closes the drawer that is now sitting over the login screen. A refusal (non-null return) must keep the drawer open and show the SnackBar; swallowing it leaves a delete button that silently does nothing.

_SettingsDrawerState._save must keep surfacing the server's own message via _nameError; the client holds no copy of the name rules (server NAME_PATTERN includes \p{M} for Indic vowel signs). Adding a client-side validator/inputFormatter will reject legitimate names the server accepts.
maxLength: 24 on the name field mirrors DISPLAY_NAME_MAX; the server truncates/refuses beyond it.

cappedBody uses `.replaceFirst('{cap}', formatChips(...))`. The {cap} token exists in all five translations — rewording the English string without the token, or switching to string interpolation, leaves a literal '{cap}' on screen in four languages.

Every visible string on this screen comes from Strings via state.t; new copy needs a key added to ALL FIVE language maps plus a getter. The only deliberate exceptions here are 'Change your picture' (tooltip), the _PrivateCard body ('Boot X, max win Y. Share the code to fill the seats.') and 'Using your <provider> picture.' — do not silently add more.

AppTheme.paletteFor(scheme, category:, bootAmount:) is the single source of a table's identity (gold seen / sapphire blind<1000 / royal purple blind>=1000) and the SAME palette paints the felt on table_screen. Recolouring lobby cards locally breaks the promise that the room matches the card that was tapped.

PremiumSurface is shared with the table screen and seat pods; changing its defaults (radius, tint, borderWidth, the three-layer shadow) redesigns the game room at the same time. The lobby passes tint: palette.tint * 0.8 and glint: !capped — the glint suppression on a capped card is meaningful, not decoration.

Avatar identity is state.avatarUrl (the GameState getter that runs absoluteUrl over a server-relative /profiles/*.svg), not user.avatarUrl directly. _PictureChoice likewise resolves through absoluteUrl. Bypassing it loads nothing on a relative path.

chooseAvatar(null) means 'use the provider photo' and is a distinct server call from chooseAvatar(id). The button is disabled only when there is no providerAvatarUrl or the account is a guest, and it is deliberately shown-but-disabled rather than hidden.

GameState.signOut and GameState.toggleTheme are passed as bare tear-offs to onPressed/onTap (Future<void> Function() used as VoidCallback). Wrapping them in a closure that awaits and then touches context needs a mounted guard — signOut switches Screen and disposes this subtree.

Corner-chip enablement is expressed twice: `enabled` chooses the colours AND `onTap: enabled ? onTap : null` blocks the InkWell. Keeping only the colour change would let a player fire a claim the server will refuse.
The 240dp left padding on _TopBar and Positioned(top: 6, left: 12) for _BonusChip are one coupled layout, not two independent numbers. Change either alone and the bonus chip lands under the avatar.

responsivenessBlockers: podW is clamped at the call site: math.min(h*0.30, w*0.155).clamp(56.0, 128.0) (table_screen.dart:461-464, duplicated at :791). The 128dp ceiling means the pod NEVER grows on a tablet; the 56dp floor means on TP_Small (640x360dp) the name renders at width*0.135 = 7.6dp and the status label at whatever labelSmall is, unrelated to either.

The status Text is the only type in the pod not derived from `width`: it uses theme.textTheme.labelSmall (an absolute size) with no FittedBox, no maxLines and no overflow handling. 'OFFLINE'/'WAITING' in Bengali or Gujarati will overflow a 56dp pod.
The name Text has maxLines: 1 + ellipsis but NO FittedBox, so it degrades by truncation rather than shrinking — and it shares its Row with the dealer badge, which steals width*0.18 + 4dp from it.
const SizedBox(width: 4) between the name and the dealer badge (seat_pod.dart:234) — the only fixed dimension inside the pod.
_Bubble's shadow: BoxShadow(blurRadius: 8, offset: Offset(0, 3)) — fixed pixels, does not scale with pod width.

Two different bubble max-widths disagree: the OverflowBox uses width * (above ? 2.1 : 1.7) while _Bubble's own BoxConstraints hardcodes maxWidth: width * 2.1 regardless of side. For rim seats the outer 1.7 silently wins.
OverflowBox maxHeight: width * 1.3 caps the bubble; combined with maxLines: 2 + ellipsis on a server message that can be 140 chars, long lines are hard-truncated at every pod size.

_cards lays cardCount PlayingCards in a Row with zero spacing at height width*0.42 and aspect 240/336 -> 0.90*width for three cards. There is no guard: a fourth card would overflow the pod's SizedBox(width: width).

No MediaQuery.textScaler handling anywhere in lib/ — every size is a raw `fontSize:`. OS font scaling will overflow the name row and the status line (the chip pill and bet pill are protected by FittedBox; nothing else is).

Felt layout hardcodes 5 seats: static const List<Offset> _places has exactly five entries, view seat 0 is special-cased to Offset(0.335, 0.00) / h*0.84 / Positioned(bottom: h*0.035), and _OwnHand is offset by podW/2 + 8 (fixed 8dp gutter).

handH = (h * 0.29).clamp(50.0, 116.0) — the viewer's own card height, clamped independently of podW, so on a tablet the pod stops growing at 128 while the hand stops at 116 and the two drift out of proportion.
_BetFlights chip size (podW * 0.22).clamp(14.0, 26.0) and the winner chip podW * 0.28 — both keyed to the already-clamped podW.

doNotTouch: _Blink._c MUST stay `AnimationController? _c` with lazy `_c ??= ...` and `_c?.dispose()`. The comment at seat_pod.dart:419-431 records a real crash: with `late final AnimationController _c = ...`, the dispose() call RUNS THE INITIALISER for every pod that never blinked; constructing a controller needs a TickerMode lookup, that lookup is illegal on a deactivated element, and the throw lands inside _InactiveElements._unmount — the tree stops being finalised half-way and surfaces later as a duplicate GlobalKey plus an _ElementLifecycle assertion, nowhere near this widget. Every table teardown hit it. Keep the null check AND keep `if (!widget.active) return widget.child;` before any access to the `_blink` getter.

The empty-seat early return must keep returning a box of EXACTLY `width`: `if (s == null || !s.occupied) return SizedBox(width: width);`. table_screen's at() wraps it in Positioned(width: podW) and offsets _OwnHand by podW/2 + 8, so SizedBox.shrink() or const SizedBox() shifts the felt layout. Drawing anything visible for an empty seat was a deliberate product decision.

`s.chips == null ? '•••' : formatChips(s.chips!)` — null means 'withheld on a blind table', not broke. Never write `s.chips ?? 0`. The server sends chips: null + chipsHidden: true precisely so the client cannot fabricate a number.

chipsHidden is a REQUIRED constructor parameter that is never read inside seat_pod.dart. It looks dead. Do not delete it without also editing table_screen.dart:477, and above all do not 'wire it up': room.chipsHidden is true for the WHOLE room including the viewer's own seat, so gating the stack pill on it would hide the viewer's own balance. The redaction is per-seat (s.chips == null), not per-room.

handLive is computed in table_screen from FOUR conditions (room.state == betting || room.state == showdown || state.showdown.isNotEmpty || state.showdownResult.isNotEmpty) and deliberately extends past the server's hand end through the winner celebration. _inHand() depends on it. Replacing it with `room.state == TableState.betting` leaves a finished hand's bet pills hanging over a table that has gone back to waiting.

The `else if` in the `below` list is exclusive on purpose: a seat shows EITHER the bet/in-pot pills OR the status line, never both. Splitting it into two independent `if`s makes 'PACKED' appear alongside a live bet.

_status() maps SeatState.packed to t.pack — even though Strings ALSO has a separate t.packed key. That is what ships in five languages; 'fixing' it changes visible copy. Any new string key must be added to all five maps plus a getter, because Strings falls back to the raw key on a miss.

progress is the COLOUR source only. The liquid level is recomputed per frame inside LiquidFill from deadlineMs vs DateTime.now(), because GameState only republishes ~once a second and a level stepping once a second looks like stuttering. Never feed `progress` into the fill. Also: the clock is drawn only when `onTurn && progress != null && deadlineMs > 0` — all three; the caller already passes progress: onTurn(s) ? progress : null, and GameState.turnProgress itself returns null unless room.state == TableState.betting.

beat = Color.lerp(primary, error, t * t) — the SQUARED term is the urgency curve (holds green, reddens sharply at the end). The same `beat` colour feeds the border accent, the _Blink glow AND the liquid. That is the contract: 'the colour alone says how long is left'. Giving the three elements different colours breaks the signal.
Accent precedence is won > onTurn > outlineVariant. A winner's pod stays primary-accented even after the turn has moved on. Do not reorder the ternary chain.
borderWidth: onTurn ? 2 : 1.2 — the 0.8dp difference is the secondary turn cue that carries when the blink is in its trough. Keep a non-glow turn indicator.

The bubble's `SizedBox(height: 0)` + OverflowBox is LAYOUT, not decoration. If the bubble occupies real height, a player speaking nudges their own pod, cards and bet chip; for the viewer (reversed) it shoves the entire column. Keep height: 0.

The bubble must remain the LAST entry in `ordered = <Widget>[...column, ?bubble]`. Both its paint order (over the cards and dealer badge, not under) and its direction depend on that single position combined with `reversed`: reversed.toList() puts it FIRST for the viewer (top, growing up) and it stays LAST for rim seats (foot of the column, growing up over their own cards).

`reversed` is true only for view seat 0 and reverses the WHOLE column, not just the bubble — the viewer's cards and bet chip stack upward so they do not run off the felt. It is coupled to the caller's placement: seat 0 is Positioned(bottom: h*0.035) while every other seat is FractionalTranslation(0, -0.5) centred.

The bubbleSide -> tail mapping is deliberately CROSSED: BubbleSide.right (a seat on the table's left, speaking rightwards) maps to _TailFrom.left, and BubbleSide.left maps to _TailFrom.right; tailUp = bubbleSide != BubbleSide.above. Getting either backwards points the tail at the wrong player.

_TailFrom.centre positions the pointer with left: 0, right: 0 + Center, while left/right use inset = width/2 - tail/2 to land under the pod (which sits half a pod-width in from the anchored edge). That inset is only correct for the matching OverflowBox alignment (bottomRight for left, bottomLeft for right). Change one without the other and the tail de-aims.

AnimatedSwitcher key ValueKey('${s.lastBet}-${s.isBlind}') — the bet figure animates ONLY because that key changes. Keying on lastBet alone kills the transition on a blind->seen switch at the same amount; adding anything volatile (a timestamp, a hand id) makes it re-animate on every one-second rebuild.

_total uses `Tween(end: s.contributed.toDouble())` with NO `begin`. That is what makes it count up from the previous value. Adding `begin: 0` makes the in-pot figure re-roll from zero on every rebuild — i.e. once a second.

The three context.watch<GameState>() calls inside _lastBet, _total and _status are what subscribe an otherwise-StatelessWidget pod to GameState's 1s ticker. _status is called TWICE per build (once as the else-if condition, once for the text). Consolidating them into one watch at the top of build is fine; removing them freezes the pod's colour and status.

`saying` is state.saidRecently[userId]?.text, whose lifetime is a Timer(GameState.bubbleFor = 4s) with a _bubbleQueue behind it and _clearBubbles() on leave/kick. The widget must keep reading it live and disappear the instant it goes null. Do not cache the last non-null text and do not add a second dismissal timer in the widget — two timers fight and queued messages get skipped.

avatarUrl arrives ALREADY absolute (the caller passes state.absoluteUrl(s?.avatarUrl)). Avatar's doc comment says 'or server-relative' but Avatar does NOT resolve relative paths. Do not move resolution into Avatar and do not pass s.avatarUrl straight through.

Avatar routes on `link.toLowerCase().endsWith('.svg')`: the 15 bundled profile pictures are SVG (SvgPicture.network), provider pictures are bitmaps (Image.network). Sending an SVG through Image.network renders nothing. Also note SvgPicture.network has only a placeholderBuilder and NO errorBuilder — a failed SVG shows blank, not the initial; Image.network has errorBuilder using the Dart 3.12 wildcard-parameter form (_, _, _).

Avatar's fallback uses `fallback.characters.first` (the characters package), not `fallback[0]` — required for emoji and for Indic names with combining marks (matching the server's NAME_PATTERN which allows \p{M}).

isMe is resolved by userId at the call site (s?.userId != null && s!.userId == state.user?.id) and isDealer by seatIndex (s?.seatIndex == room.dealerSeat — the SERVER index, not the view index). The pod must never re-derive either from its position; view seat 0 is the viewer only because seatsInViewOrder() rotated the list.

Opponents' PlayingCards are always constructed with code: null (face down) — the server never sends other players' cards. Do not add a code path here; the flip controller would become a hidden-information leak surface.
dimmed: s.status == packed || lost keeps a packed player's cards visible-but-dimmed so the seat still reads as 'was in this hand'. Removing the cards for packed players loses that.

Pod width is the felt's unit of measure. The same podW drives _BetFlights chip size (podW*0.22), the winner chip flight (podW*0.28), the viewer's own-hand offset (podW/2 + 8) and the at() clamp (w - box). Making SeatPod size itself intrinsically, or changing its width contract, desynchronises the bet-chip flight origins from the pods they fly from.

_BetFlights fires on increases in the raw Seat.contributed — the same field _total displays — keyed by room.handNo. If a redesign smooths or animates contributed in the DTO/state layer, the flights double-fire or stop firing.

The pod is width-fixed and height-flexible: SizedBox(width: width) + Column(mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min), placed by Positioned(width: box) with NO height. Any unbounded-height child (Spacer, Expanded, a Column with mainAxisSize.max) will throw.

The felt Stack in table_screen uses clipBehavior: Clip.none AND paints the pods AFTER the category tag, pot and status — that is the only reason bubbles and bet chips may overflow their Positioned box. Changing clipBehavior or the child order clips every bubble.

PremiumSurface is shared by the lobby cards, the felt itself and the pods; its ClipRRect is also what contains LiquidFill to the pod's rounded corners. Restyling it restyles three screens and can un-clip the liquid.

_Blink returns widget.child UNCHANGED when inactive — no DecoratedBox, no extra layer. Wrapping unconditionally (e.g. an always-present ring at alpha 0) adds a compositing layer to all five pods every frame.

formatChips reads module-level globals chipNumberSystem / chipUnits written only by GameState._publishNumberFormat() — requirement 34's Indian-numbering toggle. Never format money locally with NumberFormat or string interpolation; it bypasses the lakh/crore setting.

SeatPod._pod's fourth parameter `double t` is never used in the body — harmless today, but it means the squared progress value is computed in build() and thrown away. Removing it is safe; assuming it does something is not.

The literal 'YOU' string is untranslated by design (documented in CLAUDE.md 8.4 as a known still-English string), as are the wire hand names. Do not 'fix' it inside a visual redesign without adding keys to all five language maps.

doNotTouch: PlayingCard.didUpdateWidget compares ONLY null-ness (`final wasFaceUp = old.code != null; ... if (wasFaceUp == isFaceUp) return;`). Changing a face-up card's code (As → Kd) deliberately does NOT animate. If a redesign keys PlayingCard on `code`, wraps it in AnimatedSwitcher, or splits `code` into `code` + `faceUp`, every room:state that re-sends the same cards will re-flip the whole hand — the flip is the visual meaning of the SEE action (server 'see' is free and off-turn) and must fire exactly once per hand.

`_flip` is constructed with `value: widget.code == null ? 0 : 1`. Cards that arrive already face-up — showdown reveals (Reveal.cards), sideshow reveals (SideshowHand.cards), rules_sheet examples, and a resumed/rejoined seat whose cards are already seen — must NOT play the flip. Dropping that initial value makes every reveal panel animate on mount and makes a reconnect look like the player just saw their cards.

table_screen.dart:1326 wraps each own-hand PlayingCard in `_Dealt(key: ValueKey('${state.room?.handNo}-$i'), ...)`. That ValueKey is the ONLY thing that discards the previous hand's _PlayingCardState so the new hand starts face-down and re-deals. Remove it, change it to a constant, or reorder the Row and cards will stay face-up across hands or inherit the wrong flip value. RoomState.handNo is the hand identity — do not substitute an index or a UUID generated in build().

Face-down is server redaction, not decoration. seat_pod._cards() renders `for (var i = 0; i < s.cardCount; i++) PlayingCard(height: ..., dimmed: dim)` with NO code, because the server sends opponents only `cardCount` (§6.1 serializeFor). Never synthesise a code to make the back 'nicer', never render a placeholder face, never reuse the viewer's own cards for layout — that would leak hands. Same for the viewer while blind: `you.cards` is empty and the deck of three is drawn from `i < cards.length ? cards[i] : null`.

Seat.chips == null means WITHHELD (blind table, someone else's stack), NOT zero. seat_pod prints '•••'. Any restyle that reformats the stack pill as `formatChips(s.chips ?? 0)` displays a fabricated balance. The DTO comment and the server contract both depend on the null staying distinguishable.

The pod's PremiumSurface props encode game state, not taste: `accent` = scheme.primary when Seat.status == SeatState.won, else the clock colour `beat` when onTurn, else outlineVariant; `borderWidth` = onTurn ? 2 : 1.2. Border width and border colour are how a player finds whose turn it is on a 56dp pod. Flattening them to one constant removes the turn indicator.

PremiumSurface(glint: true) has exactly ONE caller: lobby_screen.dart:431 `glint: !capped`. The travelling highlight is the entry-cap signal (Requirement 30) — a glinting card is joinable, a dull one is not, and the same `capped` flag also swaps accent to outlineVariant and tint to null. Making the glint always-on, always-off, or purely decorative destroys a state signal that has no other visual carrier on that card.

PremiumSurface's internal Stack is sized by its FIRST, non-positioned child (`glint ? Glint(child: child) : child`); the bevel is a Positioned and cannot size it. In seat_pod the LiquidFill is `Positioned.fill` and the Padding/Column is the only non-positioned child. If a redesign makes LiquidFill (or any new Positioned.fill decoration) the first non-positioned child, or wraps the column in Positioned.fill, every pod collapses to zero size and the table goes blank.

Glint's LinearGradient `stops` must stay non-decreasing. centre travels -0.07 → 1.07 and each stop is `.clamp(0.0, 1.0)`; the -_halfBand/+_halfBand offsets are chosen so the band never collapses into a full-surface flash and the stops never invert. Widening _halfBand, changing the centre range, or adding a fourth stop without re-deriving the maths throws a LinearGradient assertion at runtime, not at compile time.

PremiumSurface applies a ClipRRect(radius) around its child. The felt (table_screen.dart:533, radius h/2) contains a Stack with `clipBehavior: Clip.none`, which is still clipped by that ClipRRect — the `at()` helper clamps pod positions inside the felt precisely because of it (`.clamp(0.0, max(0, w - box))`, the fix for the outermost seat being cut off on a narrow screen). Changing the felt radius, removing the clip, or changing podW changes which seats survive at the rim.

The bevel's height IS the radius. The felt passes radius: h/2, so what looks like a stray sheen over the top half of the table is the 'top bevel'. Do not 'fix' it by hardcoding a bevel height without checking the felt, and do not change the felt's radius expecting only the corners to move.

LiquidFill recomputes `_level()` from `DateTime.now().millisecondsSinceEpoch` on EVERY FRAME on purpose, and takes `deadlineMs`/`totalMs` rather than a level, because GameState republishes about once a second and a per-second level visibly stutters (§12.3: per-frame clocks compute from deadlineMs - now inside an AnimationController, never from the 1s tick). Do not 'simplify' it to accept SeatPod.progress. There is also no clock-skew correction — the fill can be ahead of or behind the server, which is tolerated because the SERVER enforces the 25s timeout, auto-packs and counts missedTurns. Nothing in the client may trigger an action when the pod fills.

LiquidFill is mounted only when `onTurn && progress != null && deadlineMs > 0`, and GameState.turnProgress returns null unless `room.state == TableState.betting` and `turn.deadline > 0`. That triple gate is what stops a stale clock from filling during SHOWDOWN or WAITING. Do not render the liquid on a cached deadline, and do not keep the pod 'on turn' through the celebration (`handLive` deliberately extends past TableState.betting for BETS and STATUSES only, not for the clock).

`_LiquidPainter.paint` returns early `if (level <= 0) return;` — before a turn starts, the pod is empty rather than showing a zero-height artefact. Removing the guard draws a full-width crest line across the bottom of every pod.

_FireworksPainter.shouldRepaint compares only `t`, `seed` and `focus` — it OMITS `bursts` and `palette`. A restyle that animates the palette or changes burst count without a t/seed/focus change will silently not repaint. (Contrast _ChipPainter and _LiquidPainter, which compare every field.) Fix it if you touch it; do not build a design that depends on the current behaviour.

Fireworks.seed must be STABLE for the whole celebration — it is `state.room?.handNo ?? 0` on the table and `won.amount` in the lobby. The pattern is regenerated from math.Random(seed*977 + b*31) on every single frame, so seeding on DateTime.now(), a Random(), or anything that changes per rebuild makes the bursts churn wildly. Two rewards of the same size looking identical is the accepted trade.

Fireworks is IgnorePointer-wrapped both internally and at every call site, and it is drawn Positioned.fill over the whole felt during the showdown overlay. If a restyle moves it out of the IgnorePointer (or gives the celebration a hit-testing background), the particles eat taps on the action bar and pods during the window where the next hand's STARTING delay (nextHandDelayMs, 4s) is already running.

The showdown celebration clears on its own timer (GameState nextHandAt, 6s fallback, §8.2) — it used to clear only on the next deal and stranded a lone winner behind the banner forever. Anything that keys the Fireworks/banner lifetime to handNo alone reintroduces that bug.

SpinningChip.initState does `Future<void>.delayed(widget.delay, () { if (mounted) _c.repeat(); })`. The `mounted` guard is required — lobby badges and store cards are created and destroyed as the rail scrolls, and _DealtState uses the identical pattern for its 110ms-per-card stagger. Removing either guard throws 'setState/ticker after dispose' on a fast leave.

SpinningChip._spinsUntil is `late final`, computed once from widget.turn/widget.rest, and _c.duration is set once in the field initialiser. Rebuilding the widget with different `turn`/`rest` values does NOT recompute either — the eased segment silently desyncs from the controller. Treat turn/rest as construction-time constants (the lobby, main.dart resume veil and update_screen each pass their own).

seat_pod's _Blink (which wraps the pod's PremiumSurface) holds `AnimationController? _c` created lazily via `_c ??= ...`, deliberately NOT `late final`. The file carries a long comment: with `late final`, `_c.dispose()` runs the initialiser for pods that never blinked, the TickerMode lookup is illegal on a deactivated element, and the throw lands inside _InactiveElements._unmount — surfacing later as a duplicate GlobalKey / _ElementLifecycle assertion nowhere near the widget. Every table teardown hit it. Anyone restyling the pod will touch this file; keep the null pattern.

PokerChip picks its rim/ring ink with `ThemeData.estimateBrightnessForColor(colour)` → Colors.white or Colors.black87. That auto-contrast is why the same painter stays legible at 16dp on a winner banner and at 46dp in the background. Hardcoding a gold rim makes light-accent chips (scheme.tertiary in light mode, AppTheme.gold) lose their dashes entirely.

LivelyChipStack's SizedBox height is `size + lift*(count-1)`, so `colours.length` is LAYOUT, not palette. chip_store.dart:474 generates `List.generate(3 + chipPacks.indexOf(p) ~/ 4, ...)` — changing the colour list length changes the shelf card's height. Its TweenAnimationBuilder(begin 0, end 1) also replays on any change of element identity (list length, key, position in the tree), so a restyle that re-keys the stack makes chips re-drop on every rebuild.

LivelyChipStack uses Curves.easeOutBack, which overshoots past 1: `-22 * (1 - landed)` becomes POSITIVE (the chip sinks below its rest position) and that is why the Opacity is written `landed.clamp(0.0, 1.0)`. Removing the clamp throws on an out-of-range opacity; adding a parent ClipRect crops the overshoot and kills the landing.

DriftingChips calls AppTheme.paletteFor(scheme, category: 'blind', bootAmount: 5000).accent — a purely decorative background depends on the table-identity palette function and on the `bootAmount >= 1000` high-stakes threshold. Change paletteFor's signature or thresholds and the ambient layer changes colour in the lobby, the table, the store and the update screen.

DriftingChips is built on a LayoutBuilder and reads box.maxHeight / box.maxWidth. Every call site places it inside a Positioned.fill or an otherwise bounded Stack. Dropping it into an unbounded Column/ScrollView gives maxHeight == Infinity and NaN positions. It is also IgnorePointer-wrapped at the CALL SITES only, never internally (table_screen.dart:70, lobby_screen.dart:58, chip_store.dart:184, update_screen.dart:36) — a new call site that forgets the wrapper makes the background swallow taps on the lobby cards and the store shelf.

DriftingChips.strength exists precisely because the table paints its felt OVER the chips and only the margins show (see the doc comment). The four literals 1.0 / 1.6 / 1.7 / 2.4 are calibrated against what is painted on top; unifying them to one constant makes the table's margins read as empty and the lobby's whisper read as noise.

PlayingCard.aspect = 240/336 is the actual viewBox ratio of assets/card_back.svg, which is drawn with BoxFit.fill (not contain). Change the constant without redrawing the SVG and every face-down card is stretched; change the SVG without the constant and backs stop matching faces. The same constant sets the SizedBox width, so it also drives how three cards fit in the own-hand row and how cardCount cards fit under a pod.

PlayingCard.rankOf / suitOf / suitSymbol are the ONLY place the server's 2-char wire codes ('As', 'Td', §6.3 deck.go) are decoded on the client. rankOf's 'T' → '10' mapping is load-bearing; suitSymbol's `_ => '?'` fallback is the visible signal that a code was misparsed — do not replace it with a blank or a default suit, or a protocol break will render as a plausible-looking wrong card.

Red/black is `suit == 'h' || suit == 'd'` painted with the theme-independent AppTheme.pipRed / pipBlack over AppTheme.cardFace (the app_theme comment: the felt and the cards are physical objects and look the same under any lighting). Re-colouring pips from the ColorScheme makes hearts/diamonds indistinguishable from spades/clubs in one of the two brightness modes — which is a rules-comprehension failure, not a style choice, on a 3-card game decided by suit-free ranking.

PokerChip is a unit of meaning, not an icon: the same painter draws the seat's last bet, the pot pile, the bet-amount stepper, the buy-chips button, the winner banner and the in-flight chips. _BetFlights and _PotToWinner position it by `size/2` and size it `(podW*0.22).clamp(14, 26)`. PremiumSurface's `elevated: false` branch (boxShadow: null) and PokerChip's `dashes` parameter have NO caller anywhere in lib/. They are inert today — do not assume they are exercised, and do not delete them assuming they are dead without checking, since they are part of the public constructor contract listed above.

The red/black split is computed from the suit letter and is how a player reads a hand before deciding. Tinting the face toward charcoal, or muting pipRed for 'restraint', degrades a game-decision input — and making cards theme-aware means a hand looks different in light vs dark mode.

TablePalette.tint IS A RAW double CONSUMED ARITHMETICALLY. lobby_screen.dart:432 does `palette.tint * 0.8`. Making it nullable, a Color, or a named enum is a compile break; raising it blends the felt further toward its accent and eats the contrast the seat pods (surfaceContainerHigh blended with THEIR own accent) depend on to stand off the felt.

THE SCHEMES ARE NOT SEED-GENERATED, despite the doc comments at app_theme.dart:6-10 and :43. There is no `keyColors`/`useKeyColors` — `_seed` #0F5236 is literally just the LIGHT scheme's `primary`, and the dark scheme's primary #7FD6A4 is unrelated. Anyone who 'just changes the seed' changes one colour in one mode. Conversely, switching FlexColorScheme into M3 key-colour generation regenerates every container and on-colour the app already depends on by name.

SeatState.won IS PAINTED WITH scheme.primary (seat_pod.dart:189-190). The winner's pod is identified by the primary colour alone. If primary is promoted to the app's general accent (used on the felt, buttons and rails), the winner stops standing out at showdown.

PremiumSurface IS THE SINGLE RAISED TREATMENT — felt, lobby cards, seat pods, sideshow prompt, sideshow reveal panel, chip store, update screen (8 call sites). It is the correct place to add frosted glass. Adding a SECOND surface widget alongside it forks the shadow/bevel/border language and the two will drift apart.

THE GLINT IS REQUIREMENT 28 ('square cards + sweep'), not decoration. Its only live use is `glint: !capped` on the lobby card (lobby_screen.dart:431) — removing it removes a stated requirement, and the capped card deliberately has it off because the card refuses the tap.

BRIGHTNESS FLIPS INSTANTLY WHILE COLOURS LERP FOR 420ms (main.dart:55-56). For that window `theme.brightness == Brightness.dark` is already the new value while every colour is mid-crossfade. Existing code only branches on brightness for alpha values, which is forgiving; branching on brightness for LAYOUT or for a hard colour choice will visibly pop on every toggle.

surfaceTintColor IS FORCED TRANSPARENT on all three button themes (app_theme.dart:132) precisely because M3 tints a raised surface by elevation and that muddies solid gold/green keys. Re-enabling surface tint for a frosted look means button colour will drift as elevation animates through the 3→6→1→0 ladder.

THEME MODE IS A PERSISTED USER SETTING WITH THREE ENTRY POINTS. GameState.themeMode ← prefs 'darkMode' (game_state.dart:198/752); toggleTheme() is wired at login_screen.dart:83, lobby_screen.dart:1478 and table_screen.dart:264, each labelled with the localised t.dayMode / t.nightMode. Committing to a dark-only premium skin means deleting a persisted preference and five-language strings from three screens — not a theme-file edit.

drifting_chips.dart:65 CALLS paletteFor WITH LITERALS: `paletteFor(scheme, category: 'blind', bootAmount: 5000)` purely to borrow the purple for one ambient chip colour. Changing the signature, the 'blind' literal handling, or the >=1000 threshold silently restyles the lobby, chip store and update-screen backgrounds.

AppTheme.light()/dark() RUN INSIDE build (main.dart:49-50) AND ThemeData EQUALITY IS WHAT STOPS A FULL-TREE REBUILD. Anything non-deterministic added to the theme (a random accent, a time-derived colour, a new object without value equality) makes every ThemeData unequal and rebuilds the whole app continuously — fatal here, because _TableScreenState.build deliberately watches nothing and the per-frame clocks (LiquidFill, countdowns) assume a stable tree.

_Felt viewer geometry: `bottom: h*0.035`, `left: _places[0].dx*w ± podW/2 + 8` — magic 8dp gap between pod and hand

_Felt overlay widths: category tag `w*0.30`, pot `w*0.34`, status `w*0.4`; pot centre hardcoded at (0.5w, 0.30h) and the pot-flight origin separately at (0.5w, 0.26h) — two different constants for the same pile
_SideRail SizedBox(width: 46) — fixed rail width on every device

_MissedTurnsStrip re-derives the felt's geometry from scratch with duplicated constants: rail 46, felt padding 24, action-bar allowance 64, 0.335, 0.30/0.155, clamp(56,128), then `maxW = (podLeft - 16 - 20).clamp(120.0, 360.0)`. Any change to rail width, felt padding or bar height silently mis-caps the pills
_MissedTurnsStrip compact breakpoint `screenW < 760` and _TopBar `box.maxWidth < 760` — two different measurement bases (MediaQuery.sizeOf vs LayoutBuilder) for the same threshold

_SideshowCountdown SizedBox(width: 260, height: 8) — fixed bar width regardless of screen
_SideshowPrompt buttons `minimumSize: Size(118, 44)`
_RevealedHand PlayingCard(height: 68), _SideshowHandCard PlayingCard(height: 62), _RulesSheet _Row PlayingCard(height: 46) — three hardcoded card heights that ignore available space
Drawer widths fixed: _TableDrawer 320, _ChatDrawer 340, _StatsDrawer 340, _SettingsDrawer 340
_Rail default width 300, _PrivateCard width 320 — the private card is a different width from the square table cards
Lobby rail height capped at `math.min(box.maxHeight, 400)`; _TableCard compact breakpoint `box.maxHeight < 330` with pad 13/20 and gap 7/12
_TopBar padding EdgeInsets.fromLTRB(240, 8, 12, 4) — a 240dp magic inset to dodge the floating _BonusChip; on a 640dp-wide phone that is 37% of the bar

Chip store: shelf SizedBox(height: 206), card SizedBox(width: 168), ribbon top-pad 34 vs 16, ChipStack size 24
_NoticeHost SnackBar `width: 420` — fixed, and floating, so on a narrow phone it is nearly the whole width and on a tablet it is lost
_RulesSheet _Row SizedBox(width: 168) for the name/note column, insetPadding 28/14
Avatar radius passed as width*0.2 inside the pod but as fixed 20/24/32 everywhere else
PlayingCard.aspect = 240/336 is a hard constant (correct, but every consumer sizes by height only)

GameConfig.fromJson makes every missing int 0, so `config.maxPlayers == 0 ? 5 : config.maxPlayers` is duplicated in GameState.seatsInViewOrder and _Felt._seatCentre — two copies of the same guard
doNotTouch: `_TableScreenState.build` deliberately subscribes to NOTHING (no context.watch). The 1s ticker rebuilding the Scaffold tears down an open drawer mid-gesture. Every child subscribes for itself. Adding a `context.watch<GameState>()` at the top of that build — the pattern used everywhere else in the app — silently breaks the chat and menu drawers.

`_BlinkState._c` is a NULLABLE, lazily-created AnimationController with `_c?.dispose()`. Four of five pods never blink and never build it. Converting it to `late final AnimationController _c = AnimationController(...)` makes dispose() RUN the initialiser on a deactivated element; the TickerMode lookup throws inside _InactiveElements._unmount and the failure resurfaces later as a duplicate-GlobalKey / _ElementLifecycle assertion nowhere near the widget. Every table teardown hit this. The same reasoning is why `_RewardCelebrationState._in` and `_PackCardState._pulse` are built in initState, not in a field initialiser.

`Seat.chips == null` means WITHHELD (blind table, someone else's seat), not zero. SeatPod renders '•••' for null. Any `?? 0`, `chips ?? 0`, or non-nullable refactor of Seat.chips leaks a false stack size to the table. Note `SeatPod.chipsHidden` and `RoomState.chipsHidden` are passed around but NEVER read inside SeatPod — the null check is the real mechanism; deleting the null branch because 'chipsHidden handles it' breaks redaction.

`You.cards` is EMPTY until the player has looked; PlayingCard treats `code == null` as face-down and its flip animation is driven purely by null→non-null in didUpdateWidget. Passing a placeholder code, pre-filling three entries, or rendering from `cardCount` for the viewer destroys both the reveal animation and the see/blind distinction.
Opponents' cards are drawn from `Seat.cardCount`, never from any card list — the server never sends them. Do not 'unify' the two hand renderers into one that takes a List<String>.

`GameState.bet()` decides chaal vs raise by `amount == steps.first` and reads `raiseIndex` clamped against `options.raiseSteps`. `onState` re-clamps `raiseIndex` to `steps.length - 1` on every snapshot and resets it to 0 on a new `handNo`. A redesign that keeps its own stepper index, or that renders the ladder from anything other than `options.raiseSteps`, will send amounts the server refuses (`invalid_bet`) — the ladder is server-computed and never client-derived.

`_ChatDrawerState._send` checks the BOOL returned by `state.sendChat(text)` before clearing the field, unfocusing and popping the drawer. Treating sendChat as void means a message blocked by the 4s cooldown still clears the composer and closes the panel — the text is silently lost.

The chat cooldown ring appears in TWO places (`_SideRail` icon and `_ChatDrawer` send key) and both read `state.canChat` + `state.chatCooldownLeft` + `GameState.chatCooldown.inSeconds`. The countdown only ticks because of GameState's 1s Timer.periodic plus a one-shot Timer at the exact expiry; a widget that stops watching GameState freezes the ring at its opening value.

`_BetFlights` is stateful and diffs `Seat.contributed` per seat in didUpdateWidget, using `handNo` to reset the baseline. It MUST keep receiving a new widget instance on every room:state publish and must not be given a key that remounts it — remounting re-seeds `_seen` from the current snapshot and the boots/bets for that hand never animate. Equally, the snapshot a player arrives to is deliberately taken as the baseline so old bets do not fly.

`_Dealt` cards are keyed `ValueKey('${state.room?.handNo}-$i')`. That key is what re-runs the deal animation on every new hand. Removing it freezes the cards after the first deal; changing its shape re-runs the animation on unrelated rebuilds.
`_PotChips` fires ONLY on increase (`if (widget.pot > old.pot)`). A refactor to `didUpdateWidget` on any change makes the pile jump when the pot resets to 0 at the hand end.

`handLive` in `_Felt` is `state == betting || state == showdown || showdown.isNotEmpty || showdownResult.isNotEmpty` and is passed into SeatPod as the gate for bets/totals. It deliberately outlives the server's table state so seats keep their bets through the winner's moment. Simplifying it to `room.state == betting` empties every seat the instant the hand ends.

The showdown overlay's lifetime is owned by `GameState._celebrationTimer` (server `nextHandAt`, else 6s), not by any widget. `_clearCelebration()` is what empties `showdown/showdownResult/winnerId/winnerName/winnerPot`. Adding a widget-local dismiss timer, or gating the overlay on `room.state == showdown`, brings back the bug where the last player at a table sat behind their own banner forever.

Both `game:showdown` and `game:handEnded` land on the same `onShowdown` handler; only the second carries `nextHandAt` and the '<winner> won N' sentence (built in game_connection.dart with its own plain-thousands grouper, bypassing formatChips/lakh). Two frames arrive per hand — the overlay must tolerate being fed twice.

`Fireworks(seed:)` must stay STABLE for the duration of a celebration (`room.handNo` at the table, `rewardWon.amount` in the lobby). Passing anything that changes per frame — a timestamp, a hashCode, `Random()` — makes the bursts re-scatter every frame.

`_RewardCelebrationState` re-runs its entrance only when `won.amount` changes (`_shownFor != won.amount`). Two consecutive rewards of the identical amount already fail to re-animate; do not make it worse by keying on something even less unique, and do not key on identity of the record (it is a fresh record each time).
`GameState.dismissReward()` is the ONLY way `rewardWon` is cleared — there is no timer. Removing the tap-to-close scrim or the button strands the overlay permanently.

`turnProgress` returns null unless `room.state == TableState.betting`, and is used ONLY for the pod's colour lerp. The actual clock level is recomputed per frame inside `LiquidFill` (and inside `_SideshowCountdown`) from `deadlineMs`/`expiresAt` against the wall clock, precisely because GameState only republishes ~1/s. Feeding either widget a level from the 1s tick makes the clock visibly stutter. There is no clock-skew correction anywhere — do not add one silently.
`SeatPod` only shows LiquidFill when `onTurn && progress != null && deadlineMs > 0`. All three conditions matter: `Turn.deadline` is sent for whoever is to act, not just for you.

`state.tableScaffold` / `state.lobbyScaffold` are GlobalKey<ScaffoldState> held on GameState so `_BackGuard` in main.dart can close an open drawer BEFORE it asks 'leave the table?'. Replacing the Scaffold, moving the key, or introducing a second Scaffold layer makes the back gesture offer to leave the table when the player only wanted to close the chat.

The table's menu and chat are ONE Scaffold `drawer` slot switched by `_LeftPanel` before opening (`_open` also calls `markChatRead()` for the chat). Splitting them into a drawer + a bottom sheet changes the back-gesture contract above and drops the unread reset.

`_confirmLeave` / `_confirmSwitch` / `_BackGuard` all compute `midHand = room.state == TableState.betting && room.you?.status == SeatState.active` to choose the warning wording. That is the condition under which leaving actually forfeits the stake — it is a money warning wearing a copy-text costume (requirement 25).

`GameState.switching` exists solely to suppress the lobby flash during `room:switch` (`onLeft` returns early while it is true). A redesign that adds its own transition state, or that renders the lobby whenever `room == null`, reintroduces the flash and can strand the player if the flag is not cleared in the `finally`.

`_armSeatCheck()` (1800ms after a warm `session:ready` with no snapshot) and the `resuming` veil are the only things that detect a dead seat after a server restart. They are state-machine, not decoration — the veil looks like a loading spinner and is not one.

`formatChips` reads two MODULE-LEVEL globals (`chipNumberSystem`, `chipUnits`) written only by `GameState._publishNumberFormat()` on language or number-system change. `_sampleIn()` in the settings drawer temporarily MUTATES the global to render a preview and restores it synchronously — making that async, memoised, or run off the build thread corrupts every money figure on screen. Abbreviation starts strictly above 100000 and gives two decimals with trailing zeros trimmed (requirement 34); the number test suite locks this.

`formatChips` is also applied to hand COUNTS in the stats drawer (handsPlayed/Won/Lost/LeftMid). That is existing behaviour a redesign will be tempted to 'fix' — changing it changes what those rows say.

`colourFor(userId, scheme)` picks from `[primary, tertiary, error, secondary, inversePrimary]` indexed by SEAT INDEX (falling back to a hash of the id for someone who has left). Hashing the id was tried and gave two of five players the same colour. If the redesign changes ColorScheme roles, chat speaker colours change with them — and `error` being in that list means a normal player can be coloured red.

`AppTheme.paletteFor(scheme, category:, bootAmount:)` is the single source of table identity used by the lobby card, the felt, the category tag and DriftingChips. The `bootAmount >= 1000` test is what makes the 5,000 blind table purple. Changing the palette in one place and not the others breaks the promise that the room matches the card you tapped.

`GameConnection.act()` mints a fresh uuid `actionId` per move for server-side idempotency; `GameState.bet/pack/see/show/askSideshow` all funnel through it. Never batch, debounce-and-reuse, or replay a move payload — the ledger's UNIQUE action_id is what stops a double charge.

`_ActionBar`'s last slot is Sideshow OR Show, chosen by `headsUp = live && options.show != null && options.show > 0`. The two can never coexist (a show needs two players, a sideshow needs three). `canSideshow` is entirely the server's verdict — never re-derive it client-side from seat counts.

`_SideshowPrompt` is rendered only when `state.sideshowIsForMe`; `_SideshowRevealPanel` only when `sideshowReveal != null && showdown.isEmpty && showdownResult.isEmpty` (the winner's banner deliberately wins the race). The reveal is server-sent to exactly two players — receiving it IS the authorisation to draw it. Do not broadcast it from the room snapshot.
`_SideshowLink` is the only sideshow information other players get, and it carries no cards by design. Adding any hand hint to it leaks.

`_MissedTurnsStrip` lives in a zero-height `SizedBox(height: 0)` + OverflowBox on purpose, so the action bar never shifts under the player's thumb as the count changes. Giving it real height moves the buttons mid-hand.

`maxBlind` in `_MissedTurnsStrip` is looked up from `config.tables` by matching category AND bootAmount, `?? 4`. A private table matches nothing and falls back to 4 — that fallback is load-bearing, not dead code.

`chip_store.dart:379` writes `state.notice = t.storeNotLive` directly, with no notifyListeners; it only reaches the screen because `Navigator.pop` rebuilds. Moving that line, or making the store dismiss asynchronously, swallows the 'store not available' message.

`_deliverPurchase` must NOT return true on a path that did not credit — returning true completes the Play transaction and throws the receipt away. Nothing in the UI may short-circuit it, and `purchasePending` (currently unused by any widget) is the hook a redesign should use rather than inventing a second flag.

`GameConnection.onCards` / `requestCards()` are wired but unsubscribed, and the `room:moved` `j['state']` branch is dead (the server sends no state there). They look like available data sources; they are not currently fed.

`main()` calls `runApp` first and `state.start()` unawaited behind the splash; the splash is held a minimum `GameState.minSplash` (1400ms) and only replaced `if (screen == Screen.splash)` — a table snapshot that arrives first must be allowed to win that race.

`GameConfig.fromJson` turns every missing int into 0, which is why `maxPlayers == 0 ? 5` guards exist in two places. Removing either guard collapses the seat ring to zero seats against an older server.
